status: wave-2 (D-014/D-016): one modifier pool, three slots, rarity by modifier count; gear scales skills by tag and never grants one

modifiers.design_purpose: The plainest survivability roll; a tester can read +12 life and know exactly what changed.
Physical mitigation on top of the base's implicit plate; stacks into the armour formula, so it is worth more early than late.

The Tyrant's answer. Also the catalyst-tempering domain, so a drop and a forge temper compete for the same slot on the same terms (D-014: catalysts target, they do not gate). Tagged resistance, not fire, so the fire weapon's roll pool stays offence.

The second resistance (D-023 slice 4): a derived stat the Frost ingot reads as beside a Vanguard. Nothing deals cold to the player yet, so it waits for a cold-breathing mob; it is on the sheet so the reading is real when one arrives. Tagged only 'reading', which no base allows, so it never rolls on gear: the plate's word.
The Ward ingot's reading beside a Vanguard (D-023 slice 4): adds to fire and cold resistance alike. Tagged only 'reading', which no base allows, so it never rolls on gear: the plate's word.

modifiers.sentence: an enemy that hits you takes {n} bleed buildup
modifiers.design_purpose: The Edge ingot's reading beside a Vanguard (D-023 slice 4): the answer to a hit. The sim says the buildup; the engine applies it to the striker when a hit lands. Tagged only 'reading', which no base allows, so it never rolls on gear: the plate's word.

modifiers.sentence: your answers to a hit reach every enemy within {n} m
modifiers.design_purpose: The Reach ingot's reading beside a Vanguard (D-023 slice 4): Barbs and every later answer to a hit reach every enemy within this many metres, not only the striker. The engine finds them. Tagged only 'reading', which no base allows, so it never rolls on gear: the plate's word.

modifiers.sentence: after a hit you move {n} faster for a moment
modifiers.design_purpose: The Haste ingot's reading beside a Vanguard (D-023 slice 4): a burst of speed after a hit, for foundry.json haste_after_hit_seconds. The sim says how much; the engine runs the clock. Tagged only 'reading', which no base allows, so it never rolls on gear: the plate's word.

A form's reaction (D-023, the flow): the skill's packet this modifier is scoped to deals this much more to an enemy carrying the status; the engine tells the sim what the struck mob carries (grammar::skillHit with target statuses). Its only tag is 'reading', which no base allows, so it never rolls on gear.

A form's bleed (D-023): flat bleed buildup on the skill's hits, whatever the skill's tags. Its only tag is 'reading', which no base allows, so it never rolls on gear: the plate's word.

The Echo form's hook: every nth cast of the skill repeats itself, free of the cooldown. The sim says n (grammar::skillEchoEvery); the engine counts casts. Its only tag is 'reading', which no base allows, so it never rolls on gear: the plate's word.

modifiers.sentence: a burning enemy it freezes takes the rest of its burn at once
modifiers.design_purpose: The Quench form's hook: when this skill's chill freezes a burning enemy, the whole remaining burn lands at once (grammar::skillQuenches; the engine's freeze hook). Its only tag is 'reading', which no base allows, so it never rolls on gear: the plate's word.

The Rime form's hook: the shatter novas this skill cashes in apply this much chill to the mobs they reach (grammar::skillNovaChill). Its only tag is 'reading', which no base allows, so it never rolls on gear: the plate's word.

modifiers.sentence: the burn it lights ticks {n} faster while the enemy moves and bleeds
modifiers.design_purpose: The Sear form's hook: a burn this skill lights ticks this much faster while the mob walks and bleeds - the chasing train pays twice (grammar::skillSear; the mob snapshots it at ignition). Its only tag is 'reading', which no base allows, so it never rolls on gear: the plate's word.

modifiers.sentence: a frozen, bleeding enemy shatters from its hit
modifiers.design_purpose: The Brittle form's hook: a spell that would never shatter cashes in a frozen, bleeding enemy with its own hit (grammar::skillBrittle; the engine runs the cascade). Its only tag is 'reading', which no base allows, so it never rolls on gear: the plate's word.
Wider cone strike: the train you can pay off in one swing grows, which is the Bulwark/Glacier dance getting easier.

The Reach ingot's reading beside a skill (D-023 slice 1): one modifier for a skill's spatial extent, whatever its delivery - an area skill's radius, a projectile's flight, a strike's reach - resolved as the 'reach' multiplier (grammar::skillReach) and applied by the engine to the delivery it owns. Its only tag besides offence is 'reach', which no base allows, so it never rolls on gear: it is the plate's word until a base is given the tag.

Flat +1 fork for every projectile skill: the orb splits again on first impact, and an Ember Bolt - which does not fork on its own - learns to. The Frost Sceptre carries one as its implicit, so the cold stat-stick is what makes projectiles train-clearers.
Increased chill buildup: the top of tier 1 crosses the three-orbs-to-freeze breakpoint down to two, which is the whole point of increased-type mods - visible thresholds.
A shattered mob reaches further down the train, making cascade chains connect across looser bunches.

Flat chill on every attack: a skill with no chill of its own gains a payload (the resolver adds before it multiplies). A Frostbite mace freezes with plain strikes and then shatters with the same strikes - the freeze-shatter sentence with no spell in it. Five area strikes at tier 1, faster on top of an orb.
The plain scaling axis for the Glacier line; deliberately smaller than the mechanic mods so a fork or a freeze breakpoint always reads as the bigger prize.

modifiers.sentence: adds {n} of the hit as cold damage
modifiers.design_purpose: The added-element reading (D-023 slice 2, owner 4 Sep 2026: every ingot reads every skill): an element ingot beside a skill of another element adds {n} of the base hit as its own cold packet (grammar::skillHit), scaled by cold gear, so a two-element hit meets a mob's resistances packet by packet and, with a Catalyst later, carries cold's status. Its only tag besides offence is 'added', which no base allows, so it never rolls on gear: the plate's word.
Scales the strikes; the Iron Mace's implicit. Redline's first rung.

modifiers.sentence: adds {n} of the hit as physical damage
modifiers.design_purpose: The added-element reading (D-023 slice 2, owner 4 Sep 2026: every ingot reads every skill): an element ingot beside a skill of another element adds {n} of the base hit as its own physical packet (grammar::skillHit), scaled by physical gear, so a two-element hit meets a mob's resistances packet by packet and, with a Catalyst later, carries physical's status. Its only tag besides offence is 'added', which no base allows, so it never rolls on gear: the plate's word.

The Vigour ingot's weak reading beside a skill (D-023 slice 2): a kill with that skill restores this much life, paid by the engine when the kill lands (grammar::skillLifeOnKill). Its only tag is 'reading', which no base allows, so it never rolls on gear: the plate's word.

modifiers.sentence: casting it grants {n} armour for a moment
modifiers.design_purpose: The Plate ingot's weak reading beside a skill (D-023 slice 2): casting that skill grants this much armour for foundry.json cast_armour_seconds; the sim says how much (grammar::skillCastArmour), the engine runs the clock and hands the armour to mitigation while it lasts. Its only tag is 'reading', which no base allows, so it never rolls on gear: the plate's word.

modifiers.sentence: an enemy carrying its status deals {n} less to you
modifiers.design_purpose: The Ward ingot's weak reading beside a skill (D-023 slice 2): an enemy carrying the status that skill applies (chill, ignite or bleed, from its payload or a modifier) deals this fraction less to you, every such ward multiplying (grammar::wardMultiplier). Beside a skill that applies no status it waits for one. Its only tag is 'reading', which no base allows, so it never rolls on gear: the plate's word.
The plain scaling axis for the fire line; scales the bolt's hit, not its burn (Burn Damage does that), so the two rolls read as different choices.

modifiers.sentence: adds {n} of the hit as fire damage
modifiers.design_purpose: The added-element reading (D-023 slice 2, owner 4 Sep 2026: every ingot reads every skill): an element ingot beside a skill of another element adds {n} of the base hit as its own fire packet (grammar::skillHit), scaled by fire gear, so a two-element hit meets a mob's resistances packet by packet and, with a Catalyst later, carries fire's status. Its only tag besides offence is 'added', which no base allows, so it never rolls on gear: the plate's word.
Increased ignite buildup: the fire line's freeze breakpoint - three Ember Bolts to ignite become two. The Ember Wand's implicit.
Scales the ignite's damage per second, not the hit: the fire build that wants to set things alight and walk away.
A longer burn is more total damage and a wider window for proliferate to find a death; the slow-fuse alternative to Burn Damage.
A burning death reaches further into the pack: the fire mirror of Shatter Radius, making chain-burns connect across looser bunches.
Flat ignite on every spell: a Frost Orb that chills and burns, a Frost Nova that sets the whole ring smouldering. The cross-element roll that lets one caster run both sentences at once.
Increased bleed buildup: the top of tier 1 turns two Rends to open a wound into one.
Scales the bleed tick, and through it the moving multiplier: the build that wounds and kites.
Faster casting is a different dance (drill through the train head-on rather than circle it); kept off movement so the dash stays a fixed rhythm.

item_bases.design_purpose: The physical stat-stick: a plain physical implicit so crafting one is a felt step up from bare hands. Rolls the physical line (damage, bleed), area, speed and the on-attack payloads - so a mace can grow Frostbite and freeze with plain strikes, but never a cold-spell mod; those stay on the sceptre.

The cold stat-stick: its implicit fork is what makes the Frost Orb a train-clearer, and its roll pool is the whole cold line, so a wrought sceptre can assemble the freeze-shatter build on its own. It grants nothing (D-016): the orb is a skill you know, the sceptre is what you scale it with.

The fire stat-stick: its implicit Kindling brings the Ember Bolt to a two-hit ignite, and its pool is the fire line plus projectile - so a wrought wand can roll Forks and make the bolt split like the orb.
Defence only; offence lives on the weapon and the charm so the three slots answer three different questions.

The build-defining slot: it may roll anything, so a keen charm is where an unexpected mod can pull a build sideways (PoE cross-pollination without sockets) - Smouldering on a cold caster, Frostbite on a mace.
Era two's sceptre (D-019): the same cold roll pool as the Frost Sceptre, but bronze holds tier three - the base that unleashes a held-back roll. It is not stronger in itself; it is roomier.
Era two's armour: a little more plate than iron and room for tier-three rolls. The number spread between metals stays small on purpose; the tier cap is the point.

design_purpose: Every modifier attaches to tags, never to a skill or a socket (D-014), and gear never grants a skill (D-016: skills are learned pages, the bar is free). applies_to ['self'] marks a character stat; anything else names the skill tags the modifier excites - so a mod written today applies to a skill found tomorrow if the tags meet. effect keys follow the resolver's increased-vs-more rule: add_* is flat (and can give a skill a payload it lacks), increased_* sums within its bucket, more_* multiplies. A base's allowed_modifier_tags is the roll pool - specific tags, never the generic offence/defence pair alone, so a sceptre cannot grow physical mods and a mace cannot grow cold-spell ones; rarity is a modifier count (plain 0, keen 1-2, wrought 3-4) and never a stat. Uniques (hand-authored, rule-bending) are the next slice. Tiers are breakpoints (D-019): a tier may carry breakpoints, extra effects the roll brings at that tier and every tier above it (tier-two cold also builds chill faster; tier three chills deeper), so a higher tier is a mechanic, not only a bigger number. tier_cap on a base is the highest tier its metal can express: a roll above the cap is held back - it speaks at the cap tier's best value and shows the rest greyed - until a Preserving Transfer moves it to a base that holds it. That is the early taste: you see what the roll could be and you know which metal unleashes it.
design_purpose_pool: The era-one pool (owner, 3 Sep 2026: 'early item mods are more defensive, or small additions to damage, outside of really lucky drops' and 'too much emphasis on forks'): every interaction modifier carries from_tier 2, so a tier-one roll - what era one's mobs drop - can only be life, armour, resistance, reach and a small damage add. Elites roll a tier higher, so the lucky drop still exists and reads as luck; era two opens the pool to everyone. The sceptres' implicit is a small cold add now, not a fork. Damage tiers step 5-10% / 15-25% / 30-45%: within the threefold budget.
